title: ACIS reader ecosystem and independent-semantics boundary
mode: deeper/broader primary-source research and plan refinement
scope: Search for open-source ACIS SAT/SAB readers beyond DWG/DXF peer libraries
Separate parser independence from geometry-kernel and consumer independence
Refine existing ACIS/AcDs and FreeCAD evidence gates without adding per-slice work
Preserve external fixture provenance and licensing constraints

sources.observation: The project lists its open-source core exchange formats separately from commercial extensions, including ACIS SAT/SAB and DXF. An unmodified open-source OCCT installation must not be assumed to parse ACIS; exact component/runtime availability and license must be recorded.

The README documents an experimental SAT/SAB parser and bounded geometry conversion. The profile documentation lists SAT 105/400/600/700, ACIS BinaryFile 21800 and selected ASM BinaryFile4 versions 22000/22300/22600/22700/22900/23200; it explicitly warns that accepted versions do not imply all geometry layouts are supported. Output geometry uses CadQuery/OCCT, so it supplies parser diversity but not an independent B-rep-kernel verdict from FreeCAD.

The repository documents source commit/blob pins, generated hashes, NIST and ezdxf corpus sources with separate notices, deterministic fetch, and a rule against unclear redistribution. This is provenance guidance only; no corpus was fetched or reused.

The add-on documents SAT/SAB and DXF modeler import, no export, and geometry limitations. Its source includes a custom AcisReader and native-part/STEP conversion paths. Source inspection shows unresolved references may be assigned null at one linking site, so this cannot be treated as a strict parser oracle without diagnostic instrumentation and complete reference-closure checks. Its geometry construction uses FreeCAD/Part and therefore shares the OCCT kernel family with FreeCAD.
FreeCAD documentation identifies OCCT as the solid-geometry kernel used to create/manage solid geometry.
CadQuery documents that it is based on the OpenCascade kernel, establishing shared-kernel limitations for cq-acis geometry outputs compared with FreeCAD.

sources.observation: The documented browse-acis path inspects and exports raw SAT/SAB content; it is not a B-rep reconstruction result.

planImpact.implementationSummary: Added two experimental open-source ACIS-reader candidates to the existing comparator map, distinguished independent parsing from independent geometry kernels, required exact profile/revision/provenance and reference-closure checks, and kept the official/native ACIS route as semantic evidence. No support or defect claim follows from documentation alone.
planImpact.nextImplementation: Continue the local implementation queue. Run any candidate ACIS-reader comparison only at the existing composed external-evidence checkpoint, with pinned profiles and scratch/already-admitted data; do not add a dependency, test, or per-slice blocker.

method.limitations: Research used mutable project-maintained GitHub pages and source listings; no peer code was cloned, built, or run, and no external sample was downloaded. cq-acis is experimental and profile-bounded. InventorLoader's published prerequisites may not match current FreeCAD platforms and its parser route requires runtime verification. The report does not qualify libdxfrw, resolve external-only gates, or establish geometry semantics.
